fields.description:
## Context

A read-based documentation audit (independently verified twice: once by the auditing agent,
once by the operator) found one consistent defect class across ~143k LOC: comments/docstrings
that were true when written and are now false -- costly for LLM agents, which treat a comment as
authoritative and burn context chasing a dangling pointer.

Scoped to 9 verified sites + a read-only census of a 10th excluded family ("Parser of record").
Behaviour-preserving only: comment/docstring corrections, 2 same-file statement moves, 1
dead-assignment deletion, 1 new self-checking test. No control-flow changes. Re-verify every
site against current origin/main before editing (audit base was 2e28d817a7e); skip+report any
site that no longer matches.

## Sites

1. `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py` ~12-30 + constant block: wrongly claims
   `_STEP_VERIFY`/`_STEP_DECIDE`/`_LLM_STEP_KINDS` mirror `gate_dispatch.py` (which defines none
   of them). Real home: `src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py` (L20/21/70). 3rd copy
   of `_LLM_STEP_KINDS` at `runs.py:393` w/ differently-worded comment. Fix: correct both
   comments to name `plan_review_recovery` as canonical, note the `runs.py` copy, preserve the
   stated reason for duplication (finalize.py stays a leaf, no back-import). Add a plain test
   (no new fixture/helper) asserting the 3-way constant equality, in the existing natural test
   home if one exists.

2. `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py`: `_NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES` has 3 members; comment names only 2
   (`identity` added by b665cff905d without updating prose), plus 4 inherited stale-2-type sites:
   a docstring in `_api.py`, `graph/_ready.py` ~92-94, `graph/_unblock.py` ~167-170,
   `_io/export_ndjson.py` ~86-88. Fix: all 5 refer to the tuple by name instead of enumerating
   members (follow `_engine_support/reads.py`'s existing correct pattern). Do not change
   `export_ndjson` behaviour.

3. reconciler dispatch-apply module: one comment cites a nonexistent allowlist symbol (sole
   repo occurrence) -- restate accurately or delete. Another claims a helper is "duplicated"
   from a sibling module but only 1 definition exists repo-wide -- delete false claim. Also
   independently check 2 further unverified audit flags in the same package naming
   `set_relationship`/`payload["links"]` and re-export claims; fix if dangling, report if sound.

4. `llm/review_kernel/decide.py`: a dead assignment falsely justified as keeping an exported,
   independently-tested function "exercised/live" when the assignment target is never read.
   Delete the statement + comment if still present. File is near the 800 LOC cap -- net change
   must not increase it.

5. `llm/workflow/interpreter.py`: `_commit_state`'s docstring falsely claims it's the sole
   chokepoint for all writes (re-verified: multiple write sites bypass it). Re-census writes
   against current source, correct the docstring to claim only what's verified -- no guessing at
   an unverified mechanism.

6. `llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`: a test slices this module's raw source between 2 named
   function definitions -- making their existence/order load-bearing, invisible to rename tools.
   Add a short comment at both ends (gate_dispatch.py and the test) naming the coupling. File is
   near the 800 LOC cap -- net change must be neutral or negative.

7. `_engine_support/next_batch.py`: (a) move a local binding + its comment above the helper that
   reads it, verifying no dependency is bound later than the new spot. (b) a `__slots__` field is
   never assigned anywhere, emitted under a different name -- a published schema field, do not
   remove. Add a comment at the init explaining retained-for-compat, matching an existing sibling
   note, mentioning the rename.

8. `_commands/fsck_recover.py`: a helper is called early in the file but defined last (module
   level, resolves fine at call time). Move the definition above its first caller.

9. `llm/plan_review/floors.py`: has appliers of the same drop-a-finding algorithm as a sibling
   function (called from 3 sites elsewhere, which explain why) but calls it from neither and
   never explains why. Determine if the omission is correct; if so add a one-line note. If NOT
   correct, that's a behavioural bug, OUT OF SCOPE for this change -- report separately, do not
   fix.

10. (Read-only, do not edit) "Parser of record": several modules carry this comment above an
    argparse factory. Pin the exact file count + line numbers, used-vs-discarded per site, and
    resolve the audit-vs-recount discrepancy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every site re-verified against current origin/main before editing; mismatches are
  skipped and reported rather than forced.
- [ ] Site 1 ships a new plain test (no new helper/fixture) asserting the 3-way constant
  mirror between `finalize.py`, `plan_review_recovery.py`, and `runs.py`.
- [ ] Sites 2-9 are comment/docstring-only plus the 2 described statement moves and the 1
  dead-statement delete; no control-flow changes anywhere.
- [ ] `decide.py` and `gate_dispatch.py` line counts are net-neutral or lower after the change.
- [ ] No new config key, env var, feature flag, CI gate, lock, autouse fixture, or test helper
  (the mechanism-delta ratchet stays clean).
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` passes with no new or increased
  entries.
- [ ] Item 10's census is reported in the commit/ticket trail with no edits to those files.
- [ ] Item 3's 2 unverified cross-references are independently checked and the verdict
  (dangling vs sound) is reported.
- [ ] Item 9: if the `floors.py` omission turns out to be a real behavioural bug, it is reported
  separately and left unfixed in this change.

## Testing

- [ ] `make verify` (lint + typecheck + import-convention + full test suite) run from inside the
  fresh worktree with the worktree's own `.venv/bin` first on PATH, and its full output captured;
  the change is pushed only once this passes.
